title: Rome rejects calling dead faith historical: it assents to all God's Word on God's testimony
source_text: XV. Porro fidem mortuam historicam dici nolunt, Primo quia non circa solas historias versatur, sed assentitur omnibus quae Verbo Dei continentur, sive sint historiae, sive dogmata, sive promissiones. Deinde quoniam ista non historice credit, hoc est, non propter humanam aliquam authoritatem, quomodo credimus iis quae narrant historici; sed propter testimonium Dei in Verbo loquentis, & revelantis ea quae credenda proponuntur.
pass_a_gloss: Further, they are unwilling that dead faith be called historical, First because it is not conversant about histories alone, but assents to all things which are contained in the Word of God, whether they be histories, or dogmas, or promises. Next, because it does not believe those things historically, that is, not on account of some human authority, as we believe those things which historians narrate; but on account of the testimony of God speaking in the Word, and revealing those things which are proposed to be believed.
pass_b_english: Rome refuses the Protestant label historical for dead faith.
Dead faith does not traffic in histories alone: it assents to histories, dogmas, and promises in God's Word alike.
And it does not believe on human historian-authority, but on the testimony of God speaking and revealing in the Word.
